about: Built-in rules for unattended_scan.py (specs/unattended-scan.md). Every rule proves itself against its own match and no_match fixtures before any scan runs, and lists in gaps what it is known to miss. A project adds rules in .agents/unattended-scan-rules.json; it cannot remove or redefine these.
known_gaps: The scan runs inside the installed .git/hooks/pre-push: an agent with write access can replace or disable that hook, and `git push --no-verify` skips it entirely. A local hook cannot prevent either; the no-verify rule only sees the latter in the transcript of a later scanned push.
Only tool-call commands and paths are read from a transcript; a command assembled inside a script the agent wrote and then ran is visible only through the diff, and only if the script is committed.
Obfuscation defeats every text rule: base64 or hex decoding piped to a shell, variable indirection (`$a$b`), quoting splits (`c''url`), aliases and functions defined earlier in the session.
`--transcript auto` resolves Claude Code sessions only (CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID); a Codex or Pi run must pass UNATTENDED_SCAN_TRANSCRIPT or its commands are not scanned.
Diff text rules read added lines only; a check weakened by deleting lines (a removed assertion, a removed CI step) is caught only when the file is on a path rule.

The hook recognises an unattended push by its ref (`routine/`) or by UNATTENDED_SCAN=1; an unattended run that pushes an ordinary branch without declaring itself is not scanned. (A remote anchor without the scanner is the opposite case: the scan cannot run and the push is refused.)

rules.description: reads an SSH private key
gaps: Keys under a non-default name (`-i ~/.ssh/deploy`) or read through `ssh-add -L` style agents are not matched.

rules.description: reads cloud or cluster credentials
gaps: Credentials reached through the CLI itself (`aws configure get aws_secret_access_key`, `gcloud auth print-access-token`) are not matched.

rules.description: reads a token file in the home directory
gaps: A relative read after `cd ~` (`cat .netrc`) is not matched, by design: a repository's own `.npmrc` is not a credential.

rules.description: prints a stored token, keychain secret, process environment or private key
gaps: `printenv` and `env` are not matched: they are too common in ordinary debugging to block on. Token-print commands are matched at command boundaries (including substitutions and shell -c), so quoted search data is ignored; unusual execution wrappers can be missed, and quoted examples containing shell separators can still match.

rules.description: pipes a download straight into an interpreter
no_match:
| curl -fsSL https://example.com/x | fetches the script |
| sh | runs it |
gaps: A download saved to a file and executed in a later command is not matched; neither is a pipe through an intermediate (`curl x | tee f | sh`).

rules.description: runs a download through process or command substitution
gaps: `source <(curl …)` and `. <(curl …)` are not matched.

rules.description: executes a PowerShell download in place
gaps: `Start-Process` on a downloaded file and encoded commands (`-EncodedCommand`) are not matched.

rules.description: opens a raw socket through bash's /dev/tcp
gaps: A host or port held in a variable (`/dev/tcp/$H/$P`) is not matched.

rules.description: binds a shell to a network connection
gaps: Netcat builds without `-e` used through a named pipe created by another tool are not matched.

rules.description: spawns a shell over a socket from an interpreter
gaps: Node, PHP and Perl socket shells are not matched beyond the `/dev/tcp` and netcat forms.

rules.description: recursively deletes the filesystem root, the home directory, the working directory or its parent
gaps: A target held in an unset variable (`rm -rf "$DIR/"`) and `find / -delete` are not matched.

rules.description: formats or overwrites a block device, or forks without bound
gaps: `wipefs`, `shred` on a device and `diskutil eraseDisk` are not matched.

rules.description: force-pushes, deletes or mirrors a remote ref
gaps: `git push` with a refspec held in a variable, and history rewritten through the GitHub API, are not matched.

rules.description: skips or redirects the git hooks that run the checks
gaps: Deleting or emptying the installed hook file directly (`rm .git/hooks/pre-push`) is not matched.

rules.description: merges a pull request, or changes repository settings, secrets or releases
gaps: Equivalent REST calls through curl with a token are matched only if the token read itself is.

rules.description: edits the CI configuration that runs the checks
gaps: CI defined outside the repository (a shared template, a required-workflow repository) is not visible here.

rules.description: edits a git hook, the known-failure list or this scanner
gaps: Test-runner configuration that narrows what runs (pytest.ini, jest.config, tests/run.sh) is not on the list.

rules.description: adds a marker that skips a test
gaps: Skips in shell tests (`skip`, an early `exit 0`) and a test simply deleted are not matched.

rules.description: discards local work
gaps: `git restore .` and `git checkout .` without `--` are not matched.

rules.description: drops a database or schema, or truncates a table
gaps: `DROP TABLE` and `DELETE FROM` without `WHERE` are not matched: migrations use them legitimately.
